Description:
In two volumes. The fourth edition improved. Vol.I: 360 pp.+13 engravings h.t. Vol.I: 432 pp.+12 engravings h.t. Printed for G. G. and J. Robinson, London, 1797.
--- Three-quarter leather binding. Sensitive hinges at the front, tight binding. Previous owner's name written at the front endpapers, pages clean, without notes or under linings. Foxing on engraving's pages – they do not affect the plates. Faded gilt lettering on spine.
The "Burlesque Translation of Homer" by Thomas Brydges (c.1710–1775) is a satirical, bawdy travesty of the first 12 books of the Iliad. It is first published in 1762 but this is the first edition to be illustrated and "improved". Published under the pseudonym "Caustic Barebones", it reimagines Homeric heroes in vulgar, humorous english contexts. Homer's Iliad set to bawdy verse achieved some popularity, and was reprinted several times, the last in 1797.

Interview with Alexia Polymenopoulou of Pelargos Bookstore, MBS

When did you get started in bookselling?
After my graduation from the University of Athens, BA in French Language and Literature, I started working as a librarian in various private libraries. Being excited to deal with old books led me to find a job at Erato Antiquarian Bookstore in Athens, where I was in charge of the french books section. Few years after, I was given the opportunity to open my own bookstore in the heart of Athens, known as Pelargos Bookstore.
Did you have any mentors in becoming a bookseller?
I did my apprenticeship under the guidance of George Papadatos, the owner of the bookstore Erato, who inspired me to develop my knowledge and love for old books.
What are your specialties as a dealer?
Due to my french studies, I like to deal more with french books. I am also excited handling rare books in greek language, such as first literary illustrated editions. Generally speaking, I love dealing with illustrated children books as well as travel books, particularly of the 19th century related to Greece. Another area that I adore is miniature and mini books.
What's the most amazing book you've ever sold?
Homer's Iliad, an edition of 1707, in greek and latin text.
What is your favorite part of being a bookseller?
First of all being a book lover myself, I have the opportunity to communicate and share the same passion with customers. In addition to that, the element of surprise and excitement anytime I touch an old book and try to discover the secrets hidden among the pages. It's a voyage that never ends.
Do you have an open storefront or have you in the past?
I am the owner of Pelargos Bookstore, downtown Athens, since 2012.
If so, do/did you have any bookstore pets?
Of course! I have my beloved cat, named Kourtina!
What is the funniest / strangest / scariest thing that ever happened in your store?
It is very funny to see the response of customers when they meet my cat, wondering, playing and hiding among the shelves.
What is your favorite bookshop (other than your own)?
Bromer Booksellers for miniature books, Shapero Rare Books, Politeia Bookstore for new editions.
What do you personally like to read? Collect?
I am a passionate collector of miniature and mini books and I like reading books about books.
What's your favorite book you personally own? Would you sell it, if the price were right?
I love an early 20th century folio edition of Aesop's Fables illustrated by Milo Winter and yes, I do sell it, because I have two copies! I will definitely keep one for myself!
What one book would you buy if price were no object?
The first edition of the Antiquities of Athens by Stuart and Revett.
If you were stranded on a desert island and could bring three books, what would they be?
Alice in Wonderland, The Little Prince, Tao Te Ching.
